clue.text: Cost of keeping a good woman

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the woman holds the other letters

parts.note: a dame is a woman, especially an older or titled one

explanation.surface: A grumble about the expense of supporting a wife or mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cost' looks like a verb but is the noun, as in 'what's the damage?'
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the bill or price you must pay is called this, as in asking how much is owed.

clue.text: A number of Romans on the way to boat

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
how means the way or manner something is done

explanation.surface: Roman travellers heading down the road to catch a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab sailing vessel with a lateen sail, so it is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Worker raised weapon outside — positive danger to trespassers

indicators.note: outside says the reversed weapon wraps round the worker
in a down clue, raised means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: arm means a weapon, as in firearm
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A labourer brandishes a weapon, clearly a threat to anyone straying onto the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' is the crossword's usual insect; 'raised' sends the weapon upwards in this down entry, giving MRA to wrap round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap set for intruders on private land is a classic hazard for anyone straying in.

clue.text: Criminal hiding note in comic

indicators.note: hiding means the comic holds the note concealed inside

parts.note: a gagster is a comedian who tells gags

explanation.surface: A crook conceals a message inside a comic book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in comic' reads as where the note is, but the comic is a person, a gagster, who hides N.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobster or member of an organised crime gang is a criminal.

clue.text: Make clear term's known

parts.note: a spell is a term or period, as in a spell in prison
out means known or revealed, as when a secret is out

explanation.surface: An instruction to explain that a term is already familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something explicitly in full detail is to make it plain to the listener.

clue.text: Sharing stripper? Nah, that's gross

indicators.note: gross as in disgusting or messed up, so the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rejects the idea of sharing a stripper as distasteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gross' looks like a moral verdict but signals the anagram of STRIPPER plus NAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint ownership or collaboration in a business is a form of sharing.

clue.text: Scandal concerning the French envoy?

parts.note: le is French for the
-gate is the suffix for a scandal, after Watergate

explanation.surface: A scandal involving France's diplomatic representative.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal representative or ambassador sent on a mission is an envoy.

clue.text: Push out foolish doubter

indicators.note: foolish suggests the letters behave senselessly and get jumbled

explanation.surface: A sceptic, foolish in the eyes of others, is pushed aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrust forward or make something stick out is to push it out.

clue.text: Do nothing in endeavour to start with the right people

indicators.note: to start with puts that combination first, before the do
in means the zero goes inside the attempt

parts.note: a try is an endeavour or attempt
O looks like zero, nothing
a do is a party, a social occasion

explanation.surface: Advice to idle at first while trying to start off with the correct crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb but is the noun for a celebration. The right is the political right; the Tories are Britain's Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conservatives are the main party of the political right in Britain.

clue.text: Having no drive, going under

indicators.note: no means the drive is left out

parts.note: going under the water and dying is drowning
Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in addresses

explanation.surface: Someone lacking motivation who is sinking or failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' reads as motivation but is the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessing something is the same as having it.

clue.text: Look back across road — that's a fast car

indicators.note: across means the reversed look spans over the road
back says the word for look is read from the end

parts.note: regard means look, as in regard closely
St is the abbreviation for Street, a road

explanation.surface: Glancing behind over the road at a speeding car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word for look into DRAGER before the road abbreviation is set within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A souped-up vehicle built for quarter-mile acceleration races is a very fast car.

clue.text: Prospect of this isn't half depressing — could be better!

definitions.text: Prospect of this isn't half depressing — could be better!

indicators.note: could be says these letters might become something else when rearranged

parts.note: a topical cryptic definition from the 2016 US election: the idea of a certain businessman in the White House was gloomy, and his surname means 'could be better' as in beat

indicators.note: half picks the front half of the word depressing

parts.note: to trump is to better or outdo, as a trump card beats others

explanation.surface: A wry groan that a prospect is very depressing and things could be better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ISNT plus DEPRE. 'isn't half' is British slang for 'very', so the whole clue is also a 2016 verdict on the election.
explanation.definitionFit: Written while Donald's election was a looming prospect many found gloomy, so the whole clue describes him.

clue.text: Gossip did this — her tongue's beginning to flow freely

indicators.note: to flow freely means the letters run loose into a new order
beginning picks out the opening letter of tongue's

explanation.surface: A gossip did this, her tongue starting to run freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to flow freely' shuffles DID, THIS, HER and T, the first letter of tongue's.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on scandalous inside information about people is to gossip.

clue.text: Appeal I made certainly gets polite response

parts.note: an appeal I made is my plea
sure means certainly, as in 'sure, go ahead'

explanation.surface: A request I made is certainly answered courteously.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the courteous phrase said when someone thanks you, so a polite reply.

clue.text: Capital invested in model planes

indicators.note: invested in means the capital is placed inside the model

parts.note: Kate Moss is a famous fashion model
Quito is the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: Money put into scale-model aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money and 'model' like a toy kit; they are a city and a supermodel.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland wooden fighter-bomber of the Second World War was an aircraft of this name.

clue.text: Look round three particular shows

indicators.note: round means the letters are taken in the opposite direction
shows means the word is on display within the clue text

explanation.surface: Someone inspects three specific performances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' looks like a noun but signals letters within 'three particular', read backwards because of 'round'.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaze closely or squint at something is to look.

clue.text: Crooked gent reported a total loss

indicators.note: reported means the phrase is as spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: wry means twisted or crooked, and a toff is an upper-class gent

explanation.surface: A dishonest gentleman reports that everything has been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for a posh gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaged beyond repair, such as a crashed car, is regarded as wholly lost.

clue.text: Planted, proved hard to avoid

indicators.note: to avoid means the hard letter is kept out

parts.note: shown means proved, as in it was shown to be true
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Something planted turned out to be difficult to steer clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeds put into the ground have been planted.

clue.text: Idiot's stolen a black jumper

indicators.note: stolen means the idiot has taken the letters into himself

parts.note: wally is British slang for an idiot
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fool has nicked a black sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is British for a sweater, but here it is a hopping marsupial. 'Idiot's' means the idiot has.
explanation.definitionFit: A small kangaroo-like marsupial that moves by leaping is a jumper.

clue.text: Prepared in a little yard not at this location

indicators.note: in means the location word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a tad means a little
there means somewhere other than here

explanation.surface: Things got ready in a tiny garden elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little yard' reads as a small garden, but splits as A, a tad, and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Being poised and ready for immediate use means being prepared.

clue.text: A disease one has contracted from rodents

parts.note: gout is a painful joint disease
one is I, and I has shortened becomes I's

explanation.surface: Someone has caught an illness from rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' looks like catching a disease but means shortened: 'I has' becomes I'S.
explanation.definitionFit: These burrowing South American animals related to guinea pigs are rodents.

clue.text: Spectre at the feast mentioned trouble at Lloyds

indicators.note: mentioned means said out loud, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: Lloyds is a British bank, so trouble there is bank woe

explanation.surface: An unwelcome presence at a dinner brings up problems at a British bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Lloyds is a major UK high-street bank.
explanation.definitionFit: In Macbeth the murdered general's ghost appears at the banquet, the original spectre at the feast.

clue.text: Ended with a polluter changing fuel

indicators.note: changing means the letters alter their order

explanation.surface: A dirty emitter ended by switching fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges ENDED, A and POLLUTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead-free gasoline, as sold in Britain, is a motor fuel.

clue.text: Almost late after hold-up — I'm annoyed

indicators.note: hold-up in a down clue means the letters are lifted to read bottom to top
almost means the word stops just short of its final letter

parts.note: tardy means late

explanation.surface: Running nearly late after a delay, someone is irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold-up' looks like a delay but means turning TARD upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild exclamation of irritation, like 'darn', expresses that one is annoyed.

clue.text: Still time? Rushed old writer's one line short

parts.note: ran means rushed

indicators.note: short means the pen is missing a letter

parts.note: a quill was the old writing pen
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Is there still time? An old author hurried and fell one line short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'yet' but is the adjective meaning calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and undisturbed, like a peaceful lake, means still.

clue.text: Bill's after that woman from EastEnders

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in post-war
her said in a Cockney accent drops the H, giving 'er

explanation.surface: A billing follows a character from the soap EastEnders.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in East London, where the H is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed notice stuck on a wall, as in 'post no bills', is a bill.

clue.text: Lost boys set free fox?

indicators.note: set free means the letters are released to move about

explanation.surface: Peter Pan's Lost Boys release a fox.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the fox as an example: a cunning person.
explanation.definitionFit: A crafty, cunning person is traditionally likened to a fox.

clue.text: Make up for going on TV

parts.note: off means going, as in 'I'm off'
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: An attempt to compensate for appearing on television.
explanation.definitionFit: To counterbalance or compensate for a loss is to make up for it.
